questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Research showing death metal gives fans joy, not violence
How to play the electric guitar in a heavy metal band
The history of heavy metal bands from Britain and the US
Why violent music should be banned from the radio and TV
questions.why: They discuss a study that found fans' main response to death metal was joy.

questions.q: How does Rob first understand Neil's question 'do you like metal?'
options: As a question about gold and silver jewellery
As a question about a band he listens to
As a question about metal objects he uses
As a joke about his old bike being rusty
questions.why: He talks about metal things he uses every day, like his toaster and bike.

options: Yes, it's his favourite music
He has never heard it
He likes it only live
No, it's not his kind of music
questions.why: He says, 'Nope. Not my cup of tea at all.'

questions.q: What was the fear about death metal's violent lyrics?
options: They would make fans stop caring about real violence
They would make fans feel sad and lonely for weeks
They would damage people's hearing at loud concerts
They would make young fans leave school early
questions.why: There was a fear it would make people desensitised to violence.

questions.q: According to the BBC News report, what are most death metal fans like?
options: Angry and aggressive, especially at concerts
Very nice people who wouldn't hurt anyone
Lonely and sad, with very few close friends
Mostly teenagers who want to annoy their parents
questions.why: It says most are very nice people who wouldn't dream of hurting anyone.

questions.q: What does Professor Bill Thompson say about many death metal fans?
options: They don't know much about music
They also like classical music
Most are musically trained
Most play in bands
questions.why: He says most are actually musically trained people.

questions.q: Which feeling does Professor Thompson say fans do NOT get from the music?
options: Empowerment
Joy
Aesthetic interest
Anger
questions.why: He says, 'But what they don't feel is angry.'

questions.q: What does Neil suggest early in the programme about people who like death metal?
options: They are exactly who you'd expect them to be
They may not be the kind of person you imagine
They are usually musicians who play in bands
They are dangerous and often get into fights
questions.why: He says the type of person who likes it 'may not be the kind of person you think'.
